name: Cai Dabiao
current_role: Co-founder and largest individual shareholder of Real Kungfu (Zhen Gongfu), Guangzhou-based Chinese fast-food chain; no confirmed current executive role
profile: Cai Dabiao (蔡达标) co-founded the Real Kungfu (真功夫) steamed-food fast-food chain, which grew from a single shop in Chang'an, Dongguan in 1990 into one of China's largest home-grown fast-food chains (570 outlets by 2014). He was its chairman; a 2018 report said he still directly held about 41.7% of the company.
interesting_fact: Real Kungfu is credited with tackling standardisation of Chinese fast food: in 1997 the company developed its own computer-controlled steam cabinet so steamed dishes could be made consistently across hundreds of outlets.
notes: Sensitive: Cai was detained in 2011 and sentenced to 14 years in 2014 in an embezzlement case amid a long shareholder dispute with co-founder Pan Yuhai; release status not confirmed in public sources found. He has no public contact channel; not a suitable outreach target without further verification.

name: Rajvi H Mariwala
current_role: Director, Mariwala Health Initiative (mental-health grant-maker); member of the Marico promoter family
profile: Rajvi (Raj) Mariwala is the daughter of Marico founder-chairman Harsh Mariwala and part of the promoter family behind the Parachute/Saffola consumer-goods group. In 2015 she co-founded with her father the Mariwala Health Initiative, which funds rights-based, community-led mental-health work across India; she also advocates for animal rights.
interesting_fact: Under her leadership MHI shifted to a psychosocial, 'nothing about us, without us' funding model; per Fortune India it partnered with 33 NGOs on 37 projects in 20 states over seven years.
deep_cut_fact: She describes philanthropy as 'an exercise in redistribution of wealth' and says MHI blended her father's focus on service-delivery innovation with her own rights-and-agency approach; early partners included iCALL counselling and the Bapu Trust in Pune bastis.
notes: Goes by 'Raj Mariwala' professionally. Best route is via MHI comms. Her public focus is mental health/queer-affirmative and animal advocacy rather than business, so podcast fit is indirect.

name: Dendi Ram Reddy
current_role: Managing Director, Sneha Farms Pvt. Ltd. (Sneha Group), Hyderabad
profile: D. Ram Reddy founded what became Sneha Group, starting with a single chicken shop ('Ram Reddy Chicken Market') and building a vertically integrated Telangana poultry conglomerate spanning feed, breeder farms, hatcheries, processing, eggs and edible-oil refining. He remains MD while son Varun Reddy Dendi is CEO; Japan's Mitsui & Co. now has a director on the board.
interesting_fact: Sneha Group says it set up India's first fully automated chicken processing facility (12,000 birds/hour) and has supplied frozen chicken to Indian defence organisations since 2012.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial journey began in 1981 with one chicken retail outlet in Malakpet, Hyderabad - the 'Ram Reddy Chicken Market' that was later rebranded Sneha Fresh Chicken.
notes: Low public profile; company contacts are general corporate ones. Son Varun Reddy Dendi (CEO) is the more public-facing executive.

name: William D. Banfield
current_role: Chief Business Officer, Rocket Companies (RKT), Detroit
profile: Bill Banfield is a 25+-year Rocket Mortgage veteran who joined in 1999 and rose through capital markets, serving as Chief Risk Officer and EVP of Capital Markets before becoming Chief Business Officer in March 2024. He oversees capital markets, mortgage servicing and government affairs - a remit that grew with Rocket's acquisition of servicing giant Mr. Cooper.
interesting_fact: He sits on the Mortgage Bankers Association board of directors, giving him a voice in national housing-finance policy alongside his Rocket role.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Rocket (then Quicken Loans) in 1999, he worked at two smaller Michigan-area lenders, MCA Mortgage and Lambrecht Mortgage Company; he holds a finance degree from Western Michigan University.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low personal public profile. IR email seen via search snippet of Rocket's IR page (site is bot-protected) - verify before use. Route media requests via Rocket's press room.

name: Megan Greuling
current_role: Reporting person on LendingTree (TREE) 10%-owner filings as co-executor of the estate of founder Doug Lebda and manager/co-trustee of related family holding entities; no public operating role found
profile: Megan Greuling appears in SEC filings (Form 3, Oct 2025; Schedule 13G amendments in 2026) as a deemed beneficial owner of LendingTree shares through Family Holdings LLC, a trust she co-trusts, and her role as co-executor of the estate of LendingTree founder Doug Lebda, who died in October 2025. She is not a LendingTree executive and has no public business profile.

name: Ashok Kumar Chaturvedi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, UFlex Ltd (Noida, India)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur Ashok Chaturvedi started a tiny manufacturing unit in 1985 that became UFlex, India's largest multinational flexible-packaging group (films, pouches, chemicals, holography, aseptic packaging, printing cylinders and packaging machines) with film plants in the US, Mexico, Poland, Egypt, UAE, Russia, Hungary and Nigeria and >US$1bn turnover. He was reappointed CMD from Feb 2024 for five years; son Anantshree is Vice Chairman/CEO of Flex Films.
interesting_fact: He is widely called the 'Father of Flexible Packaging' in India (title conferred at the Global Conference on Plastic & Packaging 2019) and also won the ET Polymers Lifetime Achievement Award 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He promises customers '3 Q's' - Quality, Quantity & Quickness - and is a cricket enthusiast who funds education and sports facilities for under-privileged children and youth.
notes: Best route is UFlex Global Corporate Communications (corpcomm@). UFlex's recycling/biodegradable packaging and energy-intensive film plants could be podcast angles.

name: Radhe Shyam Dixit
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Ananda Group / Gopaljee dairy business (Ananda Dairy), Noida, Uttar Pradesh
profile: Dr. Radhey Shyam Dixit founded the Gopaljee/Ananda dairy group, starting with a plant at Siyana, Bulandshahr (UP) in 1989. It grew into a major North Indian dairy brand selling 50+ products (paneer, ghee, milk, sweets), sourcing from 2.5 lakh+ farmers across 5,000+ village societies, with turnover of Rs 1,725 crore in FY2017-18.
interesting_fact: The group's processing capacity reached 16 lakh litres of milk a day, with over 10 lakh litres collected daily via 32 chilling centres; it also launched a dedicated 'Ananda Express' paneer salesforce in Delhi-NCR in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He set up his first factory at Siyana, Bulandshahr, on 15 November 1989 - during Phase III of Operation Flood, India's 'White Revolution' - and the company still treats that date as Ananda Group's birthday.
notes: Name spelled 'Radhey Shyam Dixit' by the company. Only a customer-care email is published; no press contact found. Web search budget ran out during this lane, so current status not re-verified beyond company site.

name: Sean McNealy
current_role: Co-Founder & Advisor, Abacus Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: ABX); 10% owner
profile: Sean McNealy is one of the co-founders (with Matthew Ganovsky and Scott Kirby) of Abacus, a life-settlements firm that went public and is now Abacus Global Management, a longevity-focused alternative asset manager with divisions in life settlements, asset management, data/tech (Abacus Intel) and lifespan-based wealth planning. He now serves as Co-Founder & Advisor and is a 10%+ shareholder.
interesting_fact: Abacus has turned life-insurance settlements - buying policies from people typically over 65 - into an institutional asset class marketed as uncorrelated with traditional markets.
notes: No longer an operating executive; low personal profile. Contact via Abacus IR. Personal biography details not verified because web search budget was exhausted.

name: Richard M Demartini
current_role: Director, Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR); Vice Chairman, Crestview Partners
profile: Richard DeMartini spent 26 years at Morgan Stanley/Dean Witter (co-president of Dean Witter, chairman of Discover Card, chairman/CEO of the international private client group), then ran Bank of America's ~$400bn wealth and asset management group (2001-04). He joined private-equity firm Crestview Partners in 2005 - which bought Victory Capital from KeyCorp in 2013 - and became vice chairman in 2021.
interesting_fact: He has served as chairman of the board of the Nasdaq Stock Market and vice chairman of the NASD, and was a founding member of Partners Capital.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee and former President and chairman of the Whitney Museum of American Art; his degree is a BA from San Diego State University.
notes: Board member, not an operator at Victory; Crestview Partners is an alternative route. Press email is Victory Capital's published media contact (Director, Global Communications).

name: Mary T Barra
current_role: Chair & CEO, General Motors; Director, The Walt Disney Company
profile: Mary Barra has run General Motors since January 2014 (chair since 2016), the first woman to lead a Detroit 'Big Three' automaker. A lifelong GM employee who started as an 18-year-old co-op student in 1980, she rose through engineering, plant management (Detroit-Hamtramck), HR and global product development; as CEO she has steered GM's push into EVs, batteries and autonomous driving.
interesting_fact: Her father was a tool-and-die maker at GM's Pontiac Motor Division for 39 years; she earned an electrical engineering degree from the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University) and a Stanford MBA on a GM fellowship.
deep_cut_fact: Her first GM job, at 18 in 1980, was as a co-op student checking fender panels and inspecting hoods at Pontiac - work she used to pay her college tuition.
notes: Extremely high-profile; requests should go through GM Global Communications (news.gm.com lists media contacts; IR site blocked automated access). Energy angle: GM's Ultium battery JV plants and EV-charging/energy (GM Energy) business.

name: Elinor Mertz
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Airbnb, Inc.; Director, DoorDash and Netflix
profile: Ellie Mertz has been Airbnb's CFO since March 2024 after 11 years in its finance organisation (head of global FP&A from 2013, VP Finance from 2019). Before Airbnb she spent 2006-2013 at Netflix in finance roles, ending as VP Finance & Investor Relations. She has sat on DoorDash's board since 2022 and joined Netflix's board in June 2025.
interesting_fact: She returned to the Netflix boardroom as a director in 2025 - 12 years after leaving the company where she had run finance and investor relations.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a CFO, her academic background is in the humanities and policy: a Stanford B.A. in Science, Technology & Society, a Stanford M.A. in History and a Columbia Master of International Affairs, in addition to a Stanford MBA.
notes: Goes by 'Ellie Mertz'. Corporate executive; outreach via Airbnb press/IR.

name: Matthew J Desch
current_role: CEO & Director, Iridium Communications (IRDM); Director, VeriSign and Unisys
profile: Matt Desch has led satellite operator Iridium since 2006 (predecessor Iridium Holdings, then the listed company from 2009), steering the $3bn Iridium NEXT constellation replacement and growth into IoT, PNT and aviation surveillance (Aireon, acquired 2026). Earlier he was CEO of Telcordia (2002-05) and spent 13 years at Nortel, including as president of its global wireless business. Iridium agreed in 2026 to be acquired by Rocket Lab.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 Iridium completed its acquisition of Aireon and won stockholder approval for its pending acquisition by Rocket Lab, which Desch called 'an important milestone in creating a next generation space powerhouse'.
deep_cut_fact: A computer-science graduate of Ohio State (MBA, University of Chicago), he sits on the President's National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee (NSTAC).
notes: Role may change on closing of the Rocket Lab acquisition - check status before outreach. Desch is an active, accessible public speaker on space/telecom; strong podcast fit.

name: Spencer Davidson
current_role: Chairman of the Board, General American Investors Company (NYSE: GAM), New York closed-end fund
profile: Spencer Davidson, 83, is a veteran New York value investor who joined General American Investors in 1994, served as its President (1995-2012) and CEO (1995-2012), and has chaired its board since 2007. Earlier he was a general partner at Beck, Mack & Oliver (1972-86), fund manager at Odyssey Partners and managing partner of the Hudson Partnership.
interesting_fact: He was lead independent director of Medicis Pharmaceutical (1999-2012) until its acquisition by Valeant, chairing its nominating/governance and compensation committees.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he served in the U.S. Army; he started his investment career at Brown Brothers Harriman in 1966 and holds a B.S. from Queens College and an MBA from Columbia.
notes: Low public profile; listed as 'Other' insider at GAM. Route via the fund's investor relations.
